decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core finishing range, it is cheap to keep as an option and one year on the market is too early to conclude that demand will not develop.

Because UV spot varnishing is more distant from the established portfolio, the abandonment risk is higher, but the firm is still likely to keep this adjacent option open for another year while market response remains uncertain.
This module builds directly on the firm's established offer and automation direction, so the option value is high and the cost of continuing to market it is likely low.
The B2 multifinisher fits the firm's core business and strategic move toward broader automated workflows, so despite its likely narrower niche it is still worth keeping on the market.
A hybrid saddle stitcher is close to the existing booklet-making and binding business, making it a natural portfolio option that the firm would usually retain at this early stage.
The add-on is closely related to the installed base and already shows a named customer application, which lowers uncertainty and makes withdrawal within the next year unlikely.
